area: NucleiSky 2D registration example: real notebooks, make_nucleisky.py fixture, N5/F3 screenshots, 2D_QC.jpg, manifest and bridge tool

facts.statement: The ideas/spec claim that NucleiSky2DApp has the structure '1 Initialise environment, 2 Load reference and query images, 3 Configure segmentation and feature extraction, 4 Perform matching, 5 Inspect the registration result'.
facts.evidence: NucleiSky/notebooks/NucleiSky2DApp/NucleiSky2DApp.ipynb (17 cells, identical on origin/main c8f8735 and local HEAD) has these markdown headings: '# NucleiSky2D App', '# Step 0: Initialize Environment & Install Dependencies', '# Step 1: Load your images and extract features' (sub-sections '### **Select Images & Configuration**' and '### **Segmentation & Feature Extraction**'), '# Step 2: NucleiSky matching' ('### **Option A: Run NucleiSky2D Matching**', '### **Option B: Run Adaptive Matching**'), '# Step 3: Apply saved NucleiSky transform'. There is no 'Inspect the registration result' heading; results appear as outputs under the Step 2 cells.

facts.statement: The real notebook has a 'Generate Random Crop' control.
facts.evidence: Cell 6 (cell index 6, 'Run to load image choosing GUI'): widgets.ToggleButtons(options=[('Load External Crop','external'),('Generate Random Crop','random')], value='external'). Random Generator Settings card: Output Size 'Height (px)' 200 / 'Width (px)' 200, Rotation 'Max Angle (°)' 180, Scaling Range 'Zoom Min' 0.7 / 'Zoom Max' 1.3, checkbox 'Fixed Seed' (False) and 'Seed Value' 42 (disabled until ticked). Default mode is Load External Crop.

facts.statement: The real notebook lets the user 'select the included example reference and query' (spec 2 demo journey).
facts.evidence: No such control or bundled data. Step 1 has a free text field 'Full Path' whose default is a hard-coded Colab/Drive path ('/content/gdrive/MyDrive/Work/manuscript/Ongoing Projects/NucleiSky/Datasets/microfluidic channel fixed/image1/Image1.tif'), a 'Crop Path' text field, and an 'Output Folder' field. The NucleiSky repo (origin/main) contains no .tif/.zarr example data at all (git ls-tree), and construct.yaml extra_files lists no data.

facts.statement: The notebook button is called 'Run matching'.
facts.evidence: Real buttons: ' Load & Process' (primary, icon play), ' Run Segmentation & Extraction' / ' Load Masks & Extract Features', ' Run NucleiSky2D' (Option A, success style, bolt icon), ' Run adaptive NucleiSky2D' (Option B, primary, rocket icon). facts.statement: make_nucleisky.py generates a 1600x1600 reference, a 520x520 query, pixel sizes 0.65 and 0.325 um/px, a 12 degree rotation, and a ground-truth JSON.
facts.evidence: LabConstrictor-Tools/fixtures/make_nucleisky.py lines 13-15 (rng seed 7, H=W=1600, PS=0.65), 17-27 (450 Gaussian blobs, sigma 5-9 px, gaussian_filter 1.0, noise 0.01, x4000 -> uint16), 29-41 (zoom 2.0, ang 12.0, 520x520, centre (cy,cx)=(800,760), bilinear map_coordinates, gain 0.9-1.1, noise sd 20), 42-43 writes reference.tif and query.tif (uint16 TIFF), 48-58 writes ground_truth.json (A_px, b_px, rotation_deg 12.0, scale 2.0, reference shape+pixel_size_um 0.65, query shape+pixel_size_um 0.325). It needs numpy + scipy + tifffile (not only numpy/Pillow). Run here with scipy 1.18.1 / tifffile 2026.9.20 installed into the scratch folder: 'ok (1600, 1600) (520, 520)' in about 1.1 s.

facts.statement: The fixture is deterministic.
facts.evidence: Two runs gave identical sha256: reference.tif 2f3e168dd174af38f09a23a6eab0622744fe53d3b38116e398b5d714851f3fee, query.tif 67ed77fcbe6850d08281825c116e710e9f7228cb4a08faec158d20aa2074cb15, ground_truth.json 14b8f149f948316aaf24cb6fae49b67c9898efa5340f197d34e08279d56b02cb. A third run with older libraries (numpy 2.1.3, scipy 1.14.1, tifffile 2025.1.10) and the NucleiSky bridge-test copy lc_tests/make_fixtures.py (a superset that also writes masks and regions) produced the same three hashes. File sizes: reference.tif 5,120,256 B (4.9 MB), query.tif 541,056 B (528 KB), ground_truth.json 433 B. uint16 ranges: reference 0-3965, query 0-3292.

facts.statement: The fixture TIFFs carry pixel-size metadata the notebook can read.
facts.evidence: TIFF tags: XResolution (1,1), ResolutionUnit NONE, ImageDescription only {"shape": [1600, 1600]}. NucleiSky get_pixel_size_um_from_tiff returns None for both files ('Could not infer XY pixel size from OME-XML or resolution tags'). In the real notebook, Load & Process with these files shows the red 'Missing Metadata' card ('Pixel size not found: Full Image, Crop Image. Please, provide the required pixel size(s) and click Load & Process again.') with fields 'Full µm/px' and 'Crop µm/px' (defaults 1.0) that must be set to 0.65 and 0.325.

facts.statement: The napari (N5) and Fiji (F3) screenshots show the same dataset as the fixture.
facts.evidence: Fiji F2 window titles read '1600x1600 (1600x1600); 16-bit; 4.9MB' and '520x520 (520x520); 16-bit; 528K' (= 5,120,256 and 541,056 bytes), names reference.tif/query.tif, pixel sizes 0.6500/0.3250. N4/N5 status line: 'done in 12.0s rotation_deg=12.1721, scale=1.0024, offset_y_px=700.3293, offset_x_px=605.5654, bbox_y0y1x0x1=[637, 963, 597, 923], n_nuclei_reference=429, n_nuclei_query=9, matcher=quad'. I ran NucleiSky's own relocalize tool function (bridge-test source 78c7f0a) on the regenerated fixture: rotation 12.17212626, scale 1.00235263, offset 700.32925837 / 605.56538305, bbox [637,963,597,923], 429/9, matcher quad, frac_inliers 1.000, mean_error_um 0.350, 10.7-14.5 s. Identical to the screenshots to every printed digit. NucleiSky lc_tests/cases.json and HUMAN_TEST_PROTOCOL Appendix A also assert 429/9 and 12.17. Ground truth offset (700.06, 606.11) and rotation 12.0 differ by up to 0.8 reference px at the footprint corners (0.12 px at the centre).

facts.statement: 2D_QC.jpg matches the fixture.
facts.evidence: NucleiSky/docs/assets/2D_QC.jpg (4276x1983, 804,508 B, added in 137e49c 2026-06-08, used only in docs/qc.md:109) is the 2x4 matplotlib QC figure of a real dense fluorescence nuclei image (about 200+ nuclei per crop, textured background), titles 'Crop (source) / Full ROI (target) / Overlay (crop->full ROI) G=Target, M=Source / Error (1-SSIM) SSIM=0.305' and, second row, 'SSIM=0.995'. The fixture crop has 9 sparse blobs. Dataset provenance is not stated anywhere in the repo (the notebook's default path suggests a 'microfluidic channel fixed' dataset: unverified). The overlay square is tilted by roughly 20 degrees by eye (unmeasured), not 12. Its SSIM=0.305 on a good alignment would confuse visitors without explanation.

facts.statement: The real NucleiSky notebook result for the fixture can be reproduced offline, so a real (not stand-in) notebook QC figure can be shown.
facts.evidence: Replicating cells 6/8/13 calls (scale_normalize_pair_for_segmentation, segment_nuclei_dispatch threshold otsu sigma 1.0 min area 80 watershed peak 5, extract_nuclear_features, run_adaptive_matching_and_export base_seed 0 margin 20, show_alignment_original_and_rescaled) with scikit-image 0.26.0, matplotlib 3.11.2, numba 0.68.0 gave 'Extracted: Full=429 nuclei, Crop=9 nuclei', matcher quad, Best Inlier Score 1.0, and wrote original_overlay.png (4273x1989, 5.2 MB) with the same 2x4 layout as 2D_QC.jpg and SSIM=0.660 (crop->full ROI) and SSIM=0.869 (full->crop). min area 5 and 80 give identical results. facts.statement: NucleiSky's reported 'scale' can be compared with the ground-truth 'scale: 2.0'.
facts.evidence: ground_truth.json scale 2.0 is the pixel zoom (query px per reference px; A_px = R/2). NucleiSky reports a calibrated micrometre-space similarity scale, 1.0024 (about 1 because both images show the same physical size). The pixel-space matrices are comparable: recovered A_px scale 0.5012 vs ground truth 0.5000 reference px per query px; A_px and b_px use the same convention in both JSON files.

findings:
SCOPE AND METHOD. Read the real notebooks cell by cell (NucleiSky app/menuinst/Welcome.ipynb, notebooks/NucleiSky2DApp/NucleiSky2DApp.ipynb, the template's Welcome_template.ipynb from LabConstrictor origin/main). Fetched refs read-only: NucleiSky origin/main is c8f8735 (only adds labconstrictor-app.yaml over the local HEAD), LabConstrictor-Tools origin/main equals the clone, the LabConstrictor clone HEAD is stale (origin/main 0066f5e used via git archive into scratch). Ran make_nucleisky.py and NucleiSky's own tool code in scratch with locally installed deps; no repository was modified. Scratch root: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/a3a6ac4f-1857-5992-b7c5-06332778d500/scratchpad/demo-feasibility/nucleisky-agent/ (fx1/ fixture, out/final/ web assets, out/nb_qc_view.png, nbpath_min80/original/original_overlay.png real notebook QC figure, real_case*.log run logs, render.py, variants.py, run_real.py, run_notebook_path.py).

HEADLINE. The fixture (make_nucleisky.py) is the SAME dataset as the napari N5 and Fiji F3 screenshots. This was verified three ways: file sizes in the Fiji title bars, the numbers in the napari status line, and an independent re-run of NucleiSky that reproduced every printed digit. So one coherent analysis can be shown across Notebook, napari and Fiji from this fixture, with REAL recorded output rather than ground-truth stand-ins. docs/assets/2D_QC.jpg is a different, real dataset and must not be mixed with the fixture numbers or inputs.

REAL NOTEBOOK FLOW (what a visitor would actually do). 1) Launch app: terminal opens, JupyterLab 4.4 opens in the browser on Welcome.ipynb. 2) Hidden code cell must be run (play button) to render the notebook table. 3) 'Open the notebook' opens NucleiSky2DApp in a NEW browser tab. 4) Step 0 cell prints either 'Local environment detected...' and a GPU line, or a CPU warning (machine dependent). 5) Step 1 'Choose Images and Output Folder': Full Path, Crop Strategy toggle, Crop Path, Output Folder, button ' Load & Process'; with the fixture TIFFs a red 'Missing Metadata' card appears and 0.65 / 0.325 must be typed into 'Full µm/px' and 'Crop µm/px', then Load & Process again: success box 'Full: 0.6500 µm/px (manual) / Crop: 0.3250 µm/px (manual)' and a matplotlib 'Full Image' / 'Crop (Target)' figure. 6) Step 1b 'Choose to apply segmentation or load existing masks': toggle 'Run New Segmentation'/'Load Existing Masks', method dropdown defaults to 'Cellpose (Deep Learning)' (needs GPU; threshold must be chosen as 'Auto-threshold (Classic CV)'), threshold panel Algorithm otsu, Channel Index 0, Blur Sigma 1.0, Min Area (px) 80, Watershed Split on, Peak Dist 5; button ' Run Segmentation & Extraction' prints 'Extracted: Full=429 nuclei, Crop=9 nuclei' and a 2x2 figure 'Full (429)' / 'Crop (9)'. 7) Step 2 Option A (' Run NucleiSky2D', 'Use default settings' checkbox, 5 tabs General/Graph Match/Quad/Triangles/Geo. Hashing, runs all four matchers) or Option B (' Run adaptive NucleiSky2D', Base Random Seed 0, accordion 'Advanced Constraints' with Export Margin (px) 20, Enable Time Limit, Max Seconds 60) producing the 2x4 QC figure. There is no sample-data picker, no 'Run matching' button, and the vocabulary is Full/Crop, not Reference/Query (napari/Fiji use Reference/Query).

PARAMETER VALUES TO SHOW AND THEIR SOURCE (all for the one recorded analysis).
Inputs (source: make_nucleisky.py / ground_truth.json, regenerated deterministically): reference.tif 1600x1600 uint16 at 0.65 um/px (field 1040 um); query.tif 520x520 uint16 at 0.325 um/px (169 um, equal to 260 reference px); query sampled 2x finer, rotated 12 degrees, centred at reference (800, 760); 450 blobs generated, 429 reference and 9 query nuclei detected.
Pixel sizes: 0.65 / 0.325 (tool defaults on bridge-test; manual entry in the notebook because the TIFFs have no metadata; N2/F2 show 0.6500/0.3250).
Segmentation (identical result 429/9 for min area 5 or 80): threshold, otsu, blur sigma 1.0, watershed on, peak distance 5; min area 5 is the tool default (N2/F2), 80 is the notebook default (cell 8); notebook default method is Cellpose, so showing threshold there means the visitor changed it. Matcher: auto (tool) = adaptive (notebook Option B, order policy for n_crop<20: quad, triangles, graph, hashing). Seed: tool unset = 0, notebook Base Random Seed 0. No time limit.
Recorded outputs (source: real run reproduced here, identical to N4/N5 text and to the Fiji Log line 'NucleiSky values: [rotation_deg:12.17212626022287, ...'): rotation_deg 12.1721, scale 1.0024 (calibrated, not the 2.0 pixel zoom), offset_y_px 700.3293, offset_x_px 605.5654, bbox_y0y1x0x1 [637, 963, 597, 923], n_nuclei_reference 429, n_nuclei_query 9, matcher quad. frac_inliers 1.000 and mean_error_um 0.350 exist only in the log and the notebook Option B box ('Best Inlier Score: 1.00'); napari and Fiji do not show them in the status line. Notebook QC figure SSIM 0.660 / 0.869 (real, computed). Timing: 12.0 s in the screenshot, 10.7-14.5 s measured here; do not display a duration as a promise. Ground truth (12.0 degrees, 2.0 zoom, b=(700.06, 606.11)) is a reference for validation, not an output.
Other real recorded outcomes available for a Matcher control: quad and hashing succeed with identical numbers; triangles and graph fail with the exact 'No match found...' message (an honest 'failed run' state). Threshold li + min area 80: 12.2927 / 1.0036 / 700.5098, 605.0372 / 425 vs 9. Blur 0, no watershed, peak 9: 12.1876 / 1.0021 / 700.4127, 605.5166 / 378 vs 8. Any other control value has NO recorded result and must not produce a fabricated one.

HOST STATUS. Only the notebook route is released: main manifest hosts [notebook], release 0.1.1 (2026-07-07) predates the bridge. The Relocalize 2D tool (tool function name relocalize, 7 outputs) exists only on the unmerged bridge-test branch, so napari/Fiji views of NucleiSky are a preview of unreleased work, consistent with the 'Experimental integration' label. The form and layers in N2/N5/F2/F3 are older than bridge-test HEAD, so a napari view built from them would omit later controls and result layers (reference_nuclei, query_nuclei, reference_outlines, query_outlines, device dropdown, slider, regions) unless the author states which version it reproduces.

VISUAL ASSESSMENT. The fixture looks like a sparse star field of blurred round blobs on black (no texture, uniform shapes); the query shows about 9 large blurry blobs because it is a bilinear 2x upsample of reference pixels. Exact overlap shows as white; there is no green/magenta fringe, so the registration is only legible with a footprint outline and a zoomed ROI inset. It is faithful to the screenshots but not a convincing tissue image; 2D_QC.jpg is more realistic but unrelated to the fixture.

DUPLICATION AND REPO-RULE POINTS. Widget labels, default values, notebook descriptions and recorded numbers in a demo would be a second hand-maintained description of Welcome.ipynb/NucleiSky2DApp.ipynb; the Welcome table already drifted (header text, typos). Per AGENTS.md (single source of truth, generated dirs git-ignored incl. docs/assets/{icons,shots,docs-img,images,hubs}, check_design enforced, no silent fallbacks) the demo data should live in one authored data file with source commit SHAs and a build-time check against the fetched notebooks, and its images in an authored folder, not a generated one. check_design.py currently allows content <button> only for copy/clear-filter (scripts/check_design.py:145-154), so demo controls need an explicit rule change.

PROVENANCE SHAs for a README: NucleiSky 2DApp notebook 5941a05 (2026-06-30); Welcome.ipynb 8a9e562 (2026-08-13, template 0.1.14); manifest c8f8735 / 935a3be (2026-10-09/10); 2D_QC.jpg 137e49c; bridge-test tool 78c7f0a (2026-10-08); Tools make_nucleisky.py 314185d (2026-10-05); screenshots N*/F* d8cb724 (2026-10-06).
risks: Showing 'select the included example reference and query' as a notebook step would misrepresent the real app: no example data ships and the notebook asks for file paths (default is a private Colab Drive path). Truthful alternatives: show the path fields filled with the fixture file names and state the files were generated by make_nucleisky.py, or use 'Generate Random Crop' (but its random angle/zoom cannot reproduce exactly 12 degrees / 2x).

Mixing 2D_QC.jpg with fixture inputs or numbers would combine two datasets in one analysis (real dense nuclei, SSIM 0.305/0.995 vs fixture, SSIM 0.660/0.869). If 2D_QC.jpg is shown at all it must be a separate, labelled illustration with unstated provenance.

Displaying the ground-truth scale (2.0) next to NucleiSky's scale (1.0024), or ground-truth values as if they were the app's result, would be wrong: they are different quantities; label ground truth explicitly or omit it.
Low SSIM values (0.660 / 0.869) on a visually perfect overlay will confuse visitors unless explained; the real notebook shows them, so cropping them out changes the real output.

Showing frac_inliers, mean_error_um or SSIM in the napari/Fiji views would be invented: those hosts show only the scalars listed in the tool declaration; frac_inliers/mean_error exist in the notebook and logs.

napari and Fiji views are previews of the unmerged bridge-test branch, not the released app (0.1.1, manifest hosts [notebook]); screenshots N2/N4/N5/F2/F3 are from 2026-10-06 and omit later controls and output layers, so building from them reproduces a stale UI.

A simulated 'Open the notebook' that switches in-page hides the real behaviour (new browser tab) and the need to press hidden play buttons; the 'Show/Hide code' toggle would reveal 168-1056 line cells, not a short snippet.

Interactive controls beyond the recorded runs (matcher, threshold method, blur, watershed, peak distance, mask use) would have to produce fabricated output; only about 7 parameter combinations have real recorded outcomes. The rest must be display-only, removed or labelled illustrative.
The Welcome intro text mentions a non-existent 'Test Connection' button, and table descriptions contain copy-paste typos; reproducing verbatim copies bugs, correcting them breaks fidelity.
